title: Finite-coefficient unbounded classical essential image
statement:
Let $k$ be a finite or algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by $\ell^r$ for some $r\geq1$. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-coefficient module sheaves, the unbounded derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and the comparison morphism $
u_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}	o X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with exact termwise inverse image $
u_X^*$ and total unbounded direct image $R
u_{X,*}$ computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex], so that $
u_X^*\dashv R
u_{X,*}$ on these unbounded categories. Write $D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the full subcategory of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are classical in the sense of [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]. Then $
u_X^*$ maps $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ into $D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, and for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, with no boundedness assumption, the counit $
u_X^*R
u_{X,*}K	o K$ is an isomorphism. In particular every object of $D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ is isomorphic to $
u_X^*M$ for some $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

proof.text: Exact inverse image commutes with each cohomology sheaf. Its sheaf image is classical by the module classical-sheaf equivalence. Transport between the chosen small and standard derived-category homology functors by their natural localization isomorphism. Thus the entire unbounded inverse image has classical cohomology.

proof.text: Set e=2*((topologicalKrullDim X).unbotD 0).toNat+1. Descend a classical fixed-ring module sheaf H to an etale sheaf G by the classical-sheaf equivalence. Realize G as a module over the constant etale ring sheaf and apply the already stated affine etale module bound at every affine etale W. A mapped injective resolution under the constant-ring equivalence and exact scalar forgetting identify this bound with ordinary fixed-ring module cohomology. The comparison of global cohomology and its pullback compatibility transfer it to R^q sections(W,H)=0 for q>e. This includes empty X and the zero coefficient ring.

It preserves countable products: choose K-injective representatives, whose termwise product is K-injective and represents the derived product; F preserves that product termwise, and exact products in ModuleCat make Q preserve it in the target. proof.text: Induct on the length of a finite cohomological interval [a,b]. The one-degree case is H^b[-b]; its derived affine sections vanish above b+e by Step 2 and shift compatibility. The truncation triangle and its long exact sequence propagate this bound. For an arbitrary classical K in degrees at most b, each tau_{>=-n}K has that bound. Pro-etale fixed-ring module sheaves have exact countable products by the proved source-library Scheme.ProEt.countableAB4Star instance, and modules have exact products. Apply the generic left-completeness truncation-bound theorem and Step 4 to obtain RF(K) in degrees at most b+e+1.

proof.text: Compute RF(K) and Rnu_*K on a K-injective representative I, using the canonical source-library rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso. Comparison direct image is restriction on etale objects. Restrict its short complex in degree q to the affine etale basis, a faithful exact functor. If each affine derived section has zero degree-q homology, the underlying presheaf short complex is objectwise exact. Exact sheafification and its natural isomorphism on sheaves make the restricted sheaf short complex exact. Faithfulness reflects exactness, so H^q(Rnu_*K)=0. This uses only objectwise vanishing and does not require constructing a natural presheaf homology comparison.

proof.text: Fix m and put n=m-e-2. The tail J=tau_{<n}K has classical cohomology and lies in degrees at most n-1. Steps 5 and 6 put Rnu_*J in degrees at most n+e, strictly below m. Its homology vanishes in degrees m and m+1. The long exact sequence of the derived image of the truncation triangle makes H^m(Rnu_*K)->H^m(Rnu_*tau_{>=n}K) invertible. Exact inverse image preserves this homology isomorphism. The upper truncation is bounded below and classical, including its zero cohomology sheaves below n. Step 3, counit naturality, and the truncation cohomology isomorphism now make H^m of the actual counit at K invertible. Vary m and apply the cohomology criterion. Take M=Rnu_*K and the counit isomorphism for the final clause.
